$comment: Gemfall beat 4 on the River Road (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 4A). The opening reads the `crossing` set from 03a through requiresFlag on two extra choices beside an ungated road: crossed_dry parties ride in with the caravans, river_took_us parties walk up from the mouth-lands and see the bent routes first (saw_the_bend, the wet door's witness dividend). Sets no carried flag. The setback needs a party that took the Pride Stone to camp alone, then fail the wolf check or pick the fight, and lose it. The expansion's spine episodes (brass rope, relay runner, cub scouts, granny cake, nap vote, moving marker, dawn moths, jackalope wall, wolf sign) set only chapter-local flags.
title: The Pride Roads

plate.narration: In the Eastern Plains, a manticore watches a road that bends far out through the grass. Fresh earth clings to the old route markers. Even the caravans are taking the long way round. Something has made pride country uneasy.

objectives.label: Saw how the pride routes bend

goal.text: Cross pride country and find out why its roads bend the long way around.

steps.label: Find what the roads bend around

facet_pride.name: The Pride Stone
facet_pride.text: From the fall no pride will den within a day of. Heavy, warm, and humming.

scene_east_bank.narration: Cross pride country and find out why its roads bend the long way around. The Eastern Plains roll away in gold grass. Ahead, the river bridge is cracked and its sky is red. Every caravan is taking a detour. The wind smells faintly of lion.

choices.label: Ride north with the crossing caravans
Squelch north out of the mouth-lands

scene_caravan_dry.narration: You fall in with the caravans coming off Stone Crossing, and there is Parsnip the donkey, with her driver, who is furious. "The pride escort wouldn't camp at the usual rest stop! Wouldn't go within a day of it! We booked them three seasons ahead!" Parsnip, who has to sleep near the gem crates, seems to agree with the prides.

choices.label: Turn off onto the pride road

scene_mouthlands_walk.narration: Walking up from the south, where nobody on the main road ever comes, you see it first: a long line of pride markers, every one pulled up and planted again in a curve. A whole road bent wide, the way you'd walk around a hot pan. In your pocket, Old Ossley's reed knot is still wet. He fished you out of the river and said, "Later. When I'm going your way." Somewhere out there, you still owe a frog a favor.

scene_pride_road.narration: Pride markers stand along the road: painted posts with tufts of tail-fur tied on top. You walk around them, never over. The detour is the point. Overhead, a cloud of embermoths drifts south, away from the mountain, which is a thing embermoths never do.

choices.label: Head for the pride on the ridge
Fly up and look at the pride routes

scene_embermoths.narration: The moths lead you along the edge of the grass, glowing like slow sparks, and the pride markers curve the same way, bending wide around something you can't see yet. Forty jackalopes have squashed themselves together along the pride edge, for safety. It is mostly ears.

scene_bend_from_above.narration: From up high the plains are a map. The pride routes used to run straight as string. Now every single one bends, wide and careful, around the same patch of grass in the middle, the way you'd tiptoe around a sleeping dog.

scene_pride_greeting.narration: A manticore elder greets you with her tail curled politely away. Somebody in a caravan faints anyway. Elder Sefa sighs. Answer the formal greeting, come home as a manticore, or let the cubs introduce you if they offered.

check_greeting.prompt: Wave first, slowly and kindly, the way the road peoples do

onSuccess.narration: Palm open, slow, from far off. The elder looks delighted, and waves you all the way up to the fire.

onFailure.narration: Everybody waves at once with both arms, like people drowning in grass. The elder blinks, decides you meant well, and lets you sit at the edge of camp.

scene_hospitality.narration: The elder sees your silhouette and drops the formal greeting completely. "Look who's come home the front way!" Cubs pile on you. Somebody's grandmother insists you eat. You are given a honeycake whether you want one or not.

scene_pride_camp.narration: "The cubs dream of humming near gem wagons," says Elder Sefa Tallgrass. "We den farther away now. Ask the centaur road-wardens. They stitch every road onto their sashes at the waystation. After the cubs' nap, I will send you there."

choices.label: Stay for the cubs' nap time

scene_riddle_account.narration: Sefa keeps a riddle account with Old Lintel, the toll-troll at Stone Crossing. Their scores have never agreed. Add his question about where a stone came from and where it is going, or risk solving their oldest riddle. Sefa has sharpened three pencils for this.

choices.label: Write the question in the ledger in your own hand

check_old_riddle.prompt: Answer the riddle nobody has solved in sixty years

onSuccess.narration: You say your answer. The whole pride goes silent. Then Sefa writes it down very carefully, and two cubs sprint off to tell everybody. You will be famous at both ends of the bridge, and argued about forever.

onFailure.narration: You guess "a teapot." It is not a teapot. Several famous careers have ended on that riddle, so you are in very good company.

scene_waystation.narration: At the centaur waystation, road maps are stitched onto sashes. This season every sash needs changing. A warden waves you to her table, spools in her mouth. Compare her lantern pattern, help prepare pinned clues, or pay a coin for prepared tags.

choices.label: Lay the sashes side by side
Help unpick and stitch a sash first
Say hello. Your letters got here first.
Pay a centaur a coin for a quick lesson in reading sashes

check_sashes.narration: The centaur with the spools in her mouth lights a lantern behind each sash, one at a time. "Quick," she says around the thread. "The new detours glow in the order the stones fell. Watch them go by, then stitch them back the same way."

interaction.cue: Watch the roads glow, then stitch them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: Sash by sash, thread by thread, you line the new detours up. The centaur takes the spools out of her mouth to say "oh."

onFailure.narration: The sashes tangle into one enormous woolly knot. The oldest centaur sighs, untangles it in about a minute, and lays them out for you, clucking her tongue.

onAssisted.narration: The oldest centaur holds the lanterns steady for as long as you need. Sash by sash, thread by thread, you line the new detours up. She takes the spools out of her mouth to say "oh."

scene_spiral.narration: Side by side, the new detours are not random. They spiral. Every road on every sash bends around the places where the stones fell, like water going around rocks. The roads are flinching. And the widest spiral of all is centered on a patch of grass a short walk from here.

choices.label: Mark every fall on the big map in red

rest_waystation.narration: The centaurs feed you oat-cakes, wrap up a supper bundle for the road, and argue about whose stitching is neatest. The barn smells of hay and new thread. Sit a while and get your breath.

choices.label: Walk out to the widest bend
Ask the pride escort to walk with you

rest_waystation_with_escort.narration: At dawn Elder Sefa walks out with you herself, and two cubs come too, because nobody told them not to. Out on the plain, the grass ahead begins to lean, just a little, away from something. Right there, Sefa stops, and the cubs stop, and nobody takes one step further. "We'll wait here," she says. "We always wait here."

choices.label: Walk on alone toward the middle

scene_widest_bend.narration: At the widest bend, a humming gem sits in a little crater. The grass leans away. So did the wolf. Taking it means the pride will keep its distance tonight; leaving it means a welcome at their fire. Decide before reaching in.

scene_take_stone.narration: The Pride Stone is heavy and warm and hums right through your fingers. When you walk back, the pride comes down off the ridge to walk with you, but further off than before. Tonight they will not camp near you. They are very sorry. They just can't.

scene_leave_stone.narration: You leave it humming in its crater. When you turn around, Elder Sefa is standing on the ridge. She bows, tail curled away, slow and deep. "Come to the fire," she says.

scene_wolves.narration: You make camp at the old caravan rest stop, among carts nobody has used since the stone fell. Your little fire is the only warm thing for miles. Out in the dark: ember eyes. A cinder wolf pack, thin and cold and a long way from home, creeping toward the heat. They do not like the humming in your packs. They like the fire very, very much.

choices.label: Chase them away from the fire
Use the long brace you learned to steady a camp windbreak

check_wolves.prompt: Throw supper far enough that the pack takes the easy meal

onSuccess.narration: The supper lands in the grass and the pack pours after it. When they come back they are full, and they lie down on the far side of the fire like big glowing dogs.

onFailure.narration: They take the supper. Then they come back for the fire.

encounter_wolves.narration: The wolves circle the old caravan carts at the rest stop, trying to get between you and the warm.

onVictory.narration: The pack backs off to a polite distance and piles up into one warm glowing heap. They are not beaten, exactly. They have just decided you are too much bother.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves want the fire more than you do, and in the end they simply have it.

rest_pride_fire.narration: Pride fire is the best fire. The cubs fall asleep on your boots, and the elders tell the story of the riddle nobody can answer. Out in the dark the gem you left hums in its crater, alone. North, tomorrow, the broken bridge.

variants.text: The marker-post brace steadied your camp cover. The pride never had to come close to the stone.
The warden helped check the pinned map. Your account includes her part.

rest_wolf_fire.narration: By midnight the cinder wolves are stacked in a glowing pile on the far side of your fire, taking turns at the bottom by some rule nobody understands. It is the warmest camp you have ever had. North, tomorrow, the broken bridge.

variants.text: The marker-post brace steadied your camp cover. The pride never had to come close to the stone.
The warden helped check the pinned map. Your account includes her part.

rest_scattered.narration: Nobody is hurt. The wolves just wanted the warm more than you did. You spend the night squashed under a cart cover, and the morning finds your camp spread across a mile of grass. It takes all day to find everything. The Pride Stone hums the whole time, as if it is not sorry at all.

variants.text: The marker-post brace steadied your camp cover. The pride never had to come close to the stone.
The warden helped check the pinned map. Your account includes her part.

scene_escort_answers.narration: You call out toward the ridge. Nothing, for a long moment. Then Elder Sefa's voice comes back out of the dark, from exactly as close as a pride will come to a humming pack and not one step nearer, and the cubs with her start a growl so low you feel it in your boots. Every ember eye on the road turns toward the ridge, thinks about it, and decides your fire is not worth the argument. The pack slinks around to the far side of your camp, as far from the pride as the warm will let them.

choices.label: Settle in, with the pride on the ridge

scene_brass_rope.narration: Six brass hats have stretched a rope across the road. The Brassbuckle Expedition is trying a toll of its own. Ask Old Lintel's question, walk around, or ask whose road this is. The rope is not attached to anything very convincing.

choices.label: Walk around the rope, the pride way
Tell them whose road this is

scene_brass_rope_ask_question.narration: "Where did you get that rope?" you ask. "And where is this road going?" The Brassbuckles look at each other. Nobody knows where the road goes. Nobody even knows where the rope came from. One of them says "Tuesday?" They take the sign down, quite quietly, and fold their stools.

scene_brass_rope_walk_round.narration: You walk around the end of the rope, the way pride folk walk around everything, slowly and politely. It turns out the rope does not stop anybody at all. It is just a rope in a field. Behind you the Brassbuckles have a long, cross talk about fences.

scene_brass_rope_whose_road.narration: "This is a pride road," you say, tail curled politely away, "and it has been since before your hats were invented." Six Brassbuckles look at you, then at each other, then at the ridge, where a lot of manticore ears have just popped up out of the grass. The rope comes down very fast indeed.

scene_relay_runner.narration: A centaur skids beside you. "Bracken Swiftmile, relay," she pants. Letters fill her sash. "News from the west? News going north? Quick. Relay waits for nobody." Ask, race, or fly her letters ahead if you can.

choices.label: Ask for news from the marsh road
Race her to the next post
Offer to fly her letters ahead

scene_relay_runner_news_west.narration: "West road's strange," says Bracken. "Marsh lights gossiping about a gate in the reeds that hums. Boggarts charging folk to cross their own puddles. And on the middle road the witches' bell charms keep ringing whenever a gem goes by." She frowns. "Everybody's stones are humming, everywhere. Funny, isn't it?" Then she is gone in a cloud of dust.

check_race.prompt: The fastest of you races a relay centaur to the next pride post

onSuccess.narration: You run like the wind, and the wind is impressed. You touch the post one breath before Bracken does, mostly because she was laughing too hard to run properly. "Fair's fair," she says, and tells you all the relay news for free: on every road in the realm, the stones are humming.

onFailure.narration: Bracken is a centaur. She reaches the post, reads her letters, eats an apple, and waves you in. "Not bad for two legs," she says kindly, and tells you the relay news anyway: on every road in the realm, the stones are humming.

scene_relay_runner_carry_letters.narration: Bracken hands over a bundle of letters for the centaur waystation up the road, where the road-wardens keep their maps, and you fly them ahead, low over the gold grass, and drop them on the big table before she has even reached the next post. When she trots in later she tells every centaur in the barn about you. Twice.

scene_cub_scouts.narration: Two rocks on the ridge are breathing. They have ears and tufted tails. Manticore cubs, pretending hard to be rocks. One giggles. Pretend not to see them, play along, or ask about the road.

choices.label: Ask them why the road bends

scene_cub_scouts_pretend.narration: You walk right past, saying loudly what a lot of nice rocks there are around here. The rocks are thrilled. They follow you all the way up the ridge, ducking whenever you turn around, and then gallop ahead to announce that they have caught some visitors all by themselves.

scene_cub_scouts_play_rocks.narration: You become rocks too. A beetle crosses a boot. "You moved!" shouts a cub. You did not. The cubs win anyway, because they made the rules.

scene_cub_scouts_ask_why.narration: "Why does the road go the long way around?" you ask the rocks. The rocks forget to be rocks. "Because of the humming," says the big one. "When we sleep near it, we dream the ground is singing," says the little one. "Grown-ups don't know why. We don't either." Then they remember they are rocks, and freeze.

scene_pride_greeting_cubs_introduce.narration: The two cubs march you up to the elder like prizes. "We caught them," says the big one. "They didn't even see us," says the little one. The elder looks at you over their heads, and you look back, and you and the elder both keep a perfectly straight face. "Then they had better come to the fire," she says.

scene_granny_cake.narration: Granny Ash, a manticore grandmother, bars the fire with a plate of spiced grass-cake. Nobody has finished a slice. The cubs want to see if you can. Granny Ash also accepts a serious interest in her recipe.

choices.label: Offer her something from your packs

check_cake.prompt: Finish a slice of Granny Ash's spiced grass-cake

onSuccess.narration: Bite. Chew. Your eyes water. Your ears go hot. Bite. Chew. You swallow the last crumb, and the whole pride roars. Granny Ash pats your head and announces to the ridge that you are family now, and nobody is allowed to argue.

onFailure.narration: Bite, chew, and steam comes out of your ears. Actual steam. You have to stop halfway and drink a whole bucket of water. Granny Ash is delighted. She has never seen anyone steam before, and she tells everybody, all evening.

scene_granny_cake_recipe.narration: Granny Ash recites ingredients. The cubs look impressed. One ingredient appears to be thunder. You ask about the timing. She asks you to pass the plates.

scene_granny_cake_share_back.narration: You dig in your packs for something to give back. As you open them, the humming gets louder, and Granny Ash takes one big step back without meaning to. Then another. She looks surprised at her own feet. "Bless me," she says. "It's not you, dear. It's whatever is singing in there."

choices.label: Close your packs and sit down

choice_cub_nap.narration: Nap time. The cubs stare at your humming packs and cannot sleep. Move the packs to study the grass outside, make a soft song together, or tell Old Lintel's story. Sefa has tried counting cubs. They keep changing places.

choices.label: Carry your packs far out of camp
Make a quiet bedtime song together
Tell them about Old Lintel and his question
Wrap the packs in Ossley's wet reed knot
Have a songkeeper start a lullaby, and everyone join in
Risk a quick song over the stones' hum

choice_cub_nap_packs_away.narration: You move the humming packs out of camp. The cubs sleep. Around the packs, grass leans away from the note. You trace its outer edge, a useful line for tomorrow, then collect the packs before leaving. Nothing from your inventory stays behind.

choices.label: Go back for the packs later

check_lullaby.prompt: Everybody sing two manticore cubs to sleep over the hum

onSuccess.narration: You sing the slowest, softest song you know, and then you sing it again. The cubs' eyes go heavy. One by one they flop over into a warm furry pile, purring, and Elder Sefa mouths a silent thank you over the top of them.

onFailure.narration: Everybody starts singing a different song at once. It is so awful that the cubs laugh until they are worn out, and fall asleep in a heap, still giggling. Elder Sefa says that counts.

choice_cub_nap_lintel_story.narration: You tell the cubs about Old Lintel, who is mostly moss, and asks everybody, "Where did you get that? And where is it going?" The cubs love it. They fall asleep asking it, in smaller and smaller voices. The last thing the little one mumbles is, "Where's it going?"

choice_cub_nap_reed_knot.narration: You wind Old Ossley's reed knot around your packs. It is still wet, of course, and as the damp creeps through, the hum goes soft, like a river running over stones a long way off. The cubs are asleep in a minute. Elder Sefa raises one eyebrow at the knot, and does not ask.

scene_moving_marker.narration: Two manticores are moving a pride marker farther from a caravan stop. Choose your part: carry its weight and learn a brace useful at tonight's camp, or study the new line to avoid tomorrow's uncertain trail search. Everyone can help plant the post afterward.

choices.label: Level the marker post between you before carrying it
Ask where the new line goes
Fly up and look at the whole line
Have a thornguard take the heavy end of the post

check_marker_post.prompt: Everybody take a corner of a pride marker post and carry it to its new hole

onSuccess.narration: You heave the post up between you and march it out to the new spot, further from the caravan road. It arrives at the hole without a wobble, tuft and all.

onFailure.narration: The post is heavier than it looks, and it looks very heavy. You wobble all the way there, and it ends up leaning against the hole like a tired giraffe.

scene_moving_marker_ask_where.narration: "Farther from the caravans," says a mover. She walks you along the old holes. You check the outward-leaning grass between them: a route you can use tomorrow without tracking uncertain prints. The post still needs planting.

scene_moving_marker_fly_line.narration: From up high you see the new hole, and the old holes, and the older holes, a long dotted line of them, each one a little further from the caravan road than the last. Something is pushing the markers out, a month at a time. You land and tell the manticores. They just nod. They know.

scene_waystation_stitch_first.narration: You choose to help pin a sash flat before comparing the roads. That takes one more job now, but leaves visible route clues instead of relying on memory. The warden removes a spool from her mouth so nobody mistakes it for a button.

choices.label: Now lay them all out together

scene_waystation_letters_arrived.narration: The whole barn turns around. "The griffin from the letters!" Somebody takes the spools out of her mouth to shake your hand. Bracken's letters are already pinned up on the wall, and the centaurs have been waiting for you so they could start the big table. They pull out a stool for everybody.

scene_spiral_mark_falls.narration: You mark the falls in red. Every road bends away from the dots. The map looks like it has measles. The oldest centaur hangs it up where everyone can see.

scene_dawn_moths.narration: At dawn, embermoths drift south in a glowing river, away from the mountain. One touches your pack and darts off. Let them pass, or try gently cupping one. The sky is orange in the wrong place.

choices.label: Stand still and let them pass
Catch one gently and look at it
Have a duskrunner dart in and cup one

scene_dawn_moths_let_pass.narration: You wait while the moths swerve around your packs. The last ones hurry south. A few small lights remain in the grass.

check_moth.prompt: Cup an embermoth in your hands without squashing it

onSuccess.narration: You cup one, as gently as a bubble. It is shivering. Embermoths love warm and love the mountain, and this one is flying away from both. You hold it till it stops shaking, then let it go, south, with all the others.

onFailure.narration: You miss. You miss again. On the third try an embermoth lands on your nose all by itself, glows very brightly, and makes you sneeze. Then it hurries south after the others, away from the mountain, as fast as it can go.

scene_jackalope_wall.narration: A wall of jackalope ears blocks the bend. They face away from its middle. Crawl carefully, ask the oldest, or spend a honeycake. The oldest has one torn ear and a very complete opinion of you.

choices.label: Crawl through on hands and knees, very politely

check_jackalopes.prompt: Everybody crawl through a wall of jackalopes without stepping on anybody

onSuccess.narration: Hands, knees, hands, knees, and "excuse me" fifty times. Not one toe is stepped on. When you come out the far side, every jackalope turns its head to watch you go, the way you watch someone walk into a cold sea.

onFailure.narration: Hands, knees, and then somebody puts a hand on a tail. One jackalope squeaks, and all fifty jump at once, straight up, like popcorn, and land again in exactly the same places. You crawl the rest of the way pink with embarrassment.

scene_jackalope_wall_ask_oldest.narration: The oldest thumps: thump, thump, pause, thump. The line opens, then closes behind you. You are fairly sure that meant "on your own head be it."

scene_jackalope_wall_honeycake.narration: You break a honeycake into fifty very small pieces. It takes ages. The jackalopes eat every crumb, very fast and very politely, and then shuffle aside to let you through. As you go, a few of the little ones try to follow, and their mothers pull them back by the ears.

scene_wolf_sign.narration: Warm paw prints cross the ash. A cinder wolf has wandered far from its usual country. Follow its outer trail, cover the prints so cubs will not follow, or use a line you already checked.

choices.label: Follow the last warm paw-print through the grass
Scuff the ash away so the cubs don't find it
Risk following the prints from a quick look
Use the outer line you already checked

check_wolf_prints.prompt: Track a cinder wolf through leaning grass

onSuccess.narration: The prints go around, and around, in a wide careful circle, and never once step toward the middle. Even a cinder wolf, which loves anything hot, has walked the long way around. The circle leads you, at last, to the very middle of the bend.

onFailure.narration: You follow the prints around and around until you realize you are following your own boot prints, following the wolf's. Embarrassing. You give up and walk straight in, and find the very middle of the bend all on your own.

scene_wolf_sign_cover_prints.narration: You scuff the warm ash into the grass until there is nothing left to see. A cub would want to follow it, and a cub should not. Then you stand up, dust off your hands, and walk on alone into the middle of the bend, where the grass leans furthest of all.

scene_waystation_lesson.narration: Your coin pays for the warden's prepared tags. "River first, then pride, bridge, pride," she says. She pins them where everyone can read the clues. You can compare instead of memorizing the lantern flashes.

choices.label: Now lay them all out together

interaction_ridge_creep.narration: The ridge path climbs through tall gold grass, and the wind comes in gusts. A pride lives up there, and a pride likes to know who is coming. The grass only hides your footsteps while it is rushing. When it goes still, so must you.

interaction.cue: Tap to creep only while the wind is rushing through the grass.

onSuccess.narration: Step, rush, freeze, step. You climb the slope without one rustle you could be blamed for.

onFailure.narration: Crunch. A twig the size of a loaf snaps under your boot. Somewhere ahead, something small and hidden snorts, the way a person does when they are trying very hard not to laugh.

onAssisted.narration: The wind rushes at just the right moments, and you climb the slope without one rustle you could be blamed for.

interaction_plates.narration: You and Granny Ash carry the plates down the pride's long table. A cub solemnly guards each slice until its owner sits down. Cake this spicy deserves an escort. Every plate arrives, and not one slice jumps off. Granny Ash tucks a honeycake into your pack. "For later," she says. "Something normal."

interaction_post_hole.narration: The post is already level from your carrying work. The movers take its weight while you guide it into the hole. Nobody lets go until the new marker stands. The post goes in straight the first time. The manticores tie a fresh tuft of tail-fur on top and say it is the neatest move all month. The smaller one pays you three coins from the pride jar. "Hole-digging wages," she says. "Do not tell the Brassbuckles."

interaction_lost_moths.narration: The glowing river has gone, but a handful of little moths got left behind. They huddle in the grass, flickering, too scared to fly south by themselves.

choices.label: Cup your hands around the glow

scene_mud_posts.narration: Two marker posts stand beside the muddy path. Nobody planted them. One blinks and burps a boot. Mire mimics. They have been collecting pride tufts and footwear, and your boots have caught their attention.

choices.label: Stomp the posts until they give up

encounter_mimics.narration: The posts pull up out of the mud on short wet legs and shuffle toward your boots. Stomp them back to being mud before they get a toehold.

scene_mimics_unmasked.narration: The mimics slump into mud and cough up boots, hats, tufts and a brave whistle. You pile the pride's tufts by the road for the cubs. The way to the bend is clear.

choices.label: Walk on toward the leaning grass

scene_mimics_took_boots.narration: The mimics win your boots. Cubs arrive with sticks and hook them back out of the mud, laughing. Hot tea follows. No whistle, but your boots and the path are safe.

choices.label: Walk on toward the leaning grass

interaction_cub_lullaby.narration: The cubs need a soft sound. Each hero adds a hum, a gentle beat or a sleepy word. Make it aloud if you like. Sefa keeps the cubs' tails from drumming on the bowls. That part is harder than it looks.

interaction_marker_load.narration: Raise or lower your end until the post is level, then carry it to the new hole. The movers show you how to brace a long load. One tuft of tail-fur keeps tickling somebody's nose. It is not helping.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side to level the marker post.

onSuccess.narration: The post reaches its hole level. You remember the long brace: it can steady a windbreak at camp.

onFailure.narration: The post is heavier than it looks, and it looks very heavy. You wobble all the way there, and it ends up leaning against the hole like a tired giraffe.

onAssisted.narration: A mover props the heavy end while you level the post. Together you learn its long brace, useful for a camp windbreak.

interaction_sash_frame.narration: Hold the cloth flat while the acting hero pins its detour tags. Alone, use the frame prop. The warden calls the landmarks as you work; the clues stay with the pinned cloth.

interaction.cue: Hold the sash flat while the acting hero pins its tags.

onSuccess.narration: The tags stay visible. Share the clues to line the roads up.

onFailure.narration: The pins slip. The warden uses her lanterns instead; watch their pattern.

onAssisted.narration: The warden holds one corner while you pin. The tags stay visible for a shared comparison.

interaction_sashes_pinned.narration: Read the pinned tags together. River, pride, bridge and another pride road belong in one account. The warden has put the spools in a cup. The cup is now the safest thing in the barn.

interaction.cue: Share the pinned clues and line up four road sections.
clues: A pride road follows the river, then the bridge road.
A second pride section is last. Use the pride tag twice.

onSuccess.narration: The four sections line up against the pins. Now the whole detour shape can be seen.

onFailure.narration: The warden corrects the pinned sections. You see the whole shape with her help, not from a checked arrangement of your own.

onAssisted.narration: The warden checks each tag beside you. Together you line up the detours.

interaction_wolf_trail.narration: The wolf's warm ash-print glows between moving grass clumps. Follow its last position. You want the wolf's outer route, not the trail your own boots have just made.

interaction.cue: Follow the warm print and choose its final position.

onSuccess.narration: You follow the outer paw-print line until the crater is in sight. The wolf never went close to its middle.

onFailure.narration: Those are your boot prints. A cub on the ridge points out the crater. You arrive with a correction, without claiming you tracked the wolf.

onAssisted.narration: A breeze parts the grass around the warm print. With that help, you follow the outer route to the crater.

scene_pride_checked_line.narration: You follow the outward-leaning grass you checked earlier. No uncertain print search is needed. At its widest curve, the line opens onto the crater.

interaction_pride_windbreak.narration: An old cart cover keeps falling into the firelight. Use the marker-post brace you learned: hold the long support while the acting hero fixes the cover. Leave a warm patch on the far side for the wolves, away from the humming packs.

interaction.cue: Hold the long brace while the acting hero fixes the windbreak.

onSuccess.narration: The cover steadies. Heat reaches the far side, and the wolves settle there. The brace you learned at the marker has made a different camp.

onFailure.narration: The cover drops. The wolves still want the fire, and you must face them.

onAssisted.narration: An old wagon wheel props the long brace. With that support, you fix the cover and leave the wolves a warm patch away from the packs.

interaction_cub_lullaby_response_hum.narration: A cub folds one ear toward the hum. The cubs settle into a furry heap. Sefa mouths thank you. Your packs still hum; the song has helped the cubs, not silenced the stones.

interaction_cub_lullaby_response_beat.narration: Sefa taps softly underneath your beat. The cubs settle into a furry heap. Sefa mouths thank you. Your packs still hum; the song has helped the cubs, not silenced the stones.

interaction_cub_lullaby_response_word.narration: A cub repeats your word into a yawn. The cubs settle into a furry heap. Sefa mouths thank you. Your packs still hum; the song has helped the cubs, not silenced the stones.

interaction_lost_moths_response_hand.narration: A moth lands on your thumb and stops shaking. The moths rise together and go south after the others, glowing steady. The grass is quiet. Ahead, the ground turns soft.

interaction_lost_moths_response_hum.narration: The moths lean toward the sound, glowing a little brighter. The moths rise together and go south after the others, glowing steady. The grass is quiet. Ahead, the ground turns soft.

interaction_lost_moths_response_dim.narration: The moths settle into the shadow, like birds into a nest. The moths rise together and go south after the others, glowing steady. The grass is quiet. Ahead, the ground turns soft.

voiceGuide.tone: wide-open, warm and a little uneasy; a homeland that is quietly rearranging itself around the stones

npcVoices.sefa_tallgrass: pride elder; voice like warm gravel; formal and kind; says 'east of the river, wave first'; quietly worried about the cubs
npcVoices.cart_driver: a caravan driver from Stone Crossing; indignant about pride escort bookings; very fond of his donkey
npcVoices.waystation_centaur: a road-warden centaur re-embroidering sashes; talks around spools of thread; tuts a great deal; precise about roads
npcVoices.brassbuckles: the Brassbuckle Expedition, six people in matching brass hats; trying out a toll rope of their own; smooth until asked a simple question
npcVoices.bracken_swiftmile: a relay-running centaur stuffed with letters; quick, cheerful, competitive; 'relay waits for nobody'
npcVoices.manticore_cubs: two manticore cubs who pretend to be rocks; giggly, honest, dream the ground is singing
npcVoices.granny_ash: a manticore grandmother with a famous spiced grass-cake nobody finishes; bossy, delighted by everything
npcVoices.marker_movers: two polite manticores moving a pride marker post further from the caravans, again

interaction_plates.narration: Granny Ash's cake is the pride's welcome, and the whole pride lines up along a long table for it. "Pass the plates down!" she calls. "Gently! Cake this spicy has opinions." The plates go hand to hand, and the cubs cheer every one.

interaction.cue: Catch the plate, then pass it down the table.

onSuccess.narration: Every plate arrives, and not one slice jumps off. Granny Ash tucks a honeycake into your pack. "For later," she says. "Something normal."

onFailure.narration: One plate wobbles, and a cub catches the cake on his head. He wears it proudly. The line laughs, and the plates go on.

onAssisted.narration: Granny Ash passes every other plate herself, and not one slice jumps off. She tucks a honeycake into your pack. "For later," she says. "Something normal."

interaction_post_hole.narration: The manticores have the post at its new hole at last, and it leans over the hole like a tired giraffe. "Hold it straight," says the bigger one, "while somebody stamps the earth in."

interaction.cue: Friends hold the post upright while someone stamps the earth in.

onSuccess.narration: The post goes in straight the first time. The manticores tie a fresh tuft of tail-fur on top and say it is the neatest move all month. The smaller one pays you three coins from the pride jar. "Hole-digging wages," she says. "Do not tell the Brassbuckles."

onFailure.narration: The post goes in slightly crooked. The manticores tilt their heads, decide crooked is fine, and tie a fresh tuft on top. "It still says keep away," one of them says.

onAssisted.narration: The bigger manticore holds the post straight herself, and it goes in first time. They tie a fresh tuft of tail-fur on top, and the smaller one pays you three coins from the pride jar. "Hole-digging wages," she says. "Do not tell the Brassbuckles."

interaction_cub_lullaby.narration: The cubs need a soft sound. Each hero adds a hum, a gentle beat or a sleepy word. Make it aloud if you like. Sefa keeps the cubs' tails from drumming on the bowls. That part is harder than it looks.

interaction.cue: Each hero adds something to the bedtime song.

options.label: Hum softly
options.reaction: A cub folds one ear toward the hum.

options.label: Tap a very gentle beat
options.reaction: Sefa taps softly underneath your beat.

options.label: Offer a sleepy word
options.reaction: A cub repeats your word into a yawn.

onSuccess.narration: The cubs settle into a furry heap. Sefa mouths thank you. Your packs still hum; the song has helped the cubs, not silenced the stones.

onFailure.narration: Sefa joins the song until the cubs settle.

onAssisted.narration: Sefa holds the tune while you add quiet sounds. The cubs sleep with everyone's help.

interaction_lost_moths.narration: The glowing river has gone, but a handful of little moths got left behind. They huddle in the grass, flickering, too scared to fly south by themselves.

interaction.cue: Help the lost moths feel safe until they glow steady again.

options.label: Hold out a warm hand
options.reaction: A moth lands on your thumb and stops shaking.

options.label: Hum very softly
options.reaction: The moths lean toward the sound, glowing a little brighter.

options.label: Cup your hands around the glow
options.reaction: The moths settle into the shadow, like birds into a nest.

stages: They lift off together, heading south.

onSuccess.narration: The moths rise together and go south after the others, glowing steady. The grass is quiet. Ahead, the ground turns soft.

onFailure.narration: The moths rise together and go south after the others, glowing steady. The grass is quiet. Ahead, the ground turns soft.
